message.content:
Here are some of the most popular and highly regarded sushi spots in Tokyo, ranging from Michelin‑starred establishments to beloved local favorites:

| Restaurant | Location | Highlights | Notes |
|------------|----------|------------|-------|
| **Sukiyabashi Jiro** | Ginza (Tokyo 3‑Star Michelin) | Legendary chef Jiro Ono, traditional Edomae sushi | Very expensive, requires advance reservations (often months ahead). |
| **Sushi Saito** | Minato | 3‑Star Michelin, intimate 10‑seat setting | Extremely hard to book; often requires a personal connection or a very early reservation. |
| **Sushi Yoshitake** | Ginza | 3‑Star Michelin, meticulous presentation | Reservations open 30 days in advance; no walk‑ins. |
| **Sushi Dai** | Tsukiji Outer Market | Fresh fish, long lines but worth it | No reservations; arrive early (before 8 am) to secure a seat. |
| **Sushi Daiwa** | Tsukiji | Similar to Sushi Dai, slightly less crowded | Also no reservations; early arrival recommended. |
| **Sushi Zanmai** | Multiple locations (Shibuya, Shinjuku, etc.) | Casual, all‑day service, affordable | Great for a quick bite; no reservations needed. |
| **Sushi Kyubey** | Ginza | 2‑Star Michelin, classic Edomae style | Reservations required; offers a “Kyubey Experience” tasting menu. |
| **Sushi Sugita** | Ginza | 2‑Star Michelin, small, intimate | Reservations needed; known for its seasonal menu. |
| **Sushi Masuda** | Ginza | 1‑Star Michelin, high quality at a lower price point | Reservations recommended; offers a lunch set. |
| **Sushi Iwa** | Roppongi | 1‑Star Michelin, modern twist on traditional sushi | Reservations needed; offers a lunch menu. |
| **Sushi Kanda** | Minato | 3‑Star Michelin, small 12‑seat counter | Reservations required; offers a tasting menu. |
| **Sushi Shimizu** | Ginza | 2‑Star Michelin, known for its omakase | Reservations needed; offers a lunch set. |
| **Sushi Tsubaki** | Ginza | 1‑Star Michelin, elegant setting | Reservations required; offers a lunch set. |
| **Sushi Saito** | Minato | 3‑Star Michelin, intimate 10‑seat setting | Extremely hard to book; often requires a personal connection or a very early reservation. |
| **Sushi Noda** | Ginza | 1‑Star Michelin, known for its fresh fish | Reservations needed; offers a lunch set. |

> **Quick‑pick options**  
> • **Sushi Iwa** – 1‑Star Michelin, modern twist, great lunch set  
> • **Sushi Masuda** – 1‑Star Michelin, affordable lunch set  
> • **Sushi Shimizu** – 2‑Star Michelin, elegant omakase  
> • **Sushi Kyubey** – 2‑Star Michelin, classic Edomae, lunch set available  

> **Tips for booking**  
> • For Michelin‑starred places, book as far in advance as possible (some accept reservations up to 90 days ahead).  
> • Many restaurants offer a *lunch set* (usually around ¥5,000–¥10,000) which is a great way to experience high‑quality sushi at a lower cost.  
> • If you’re flexible, consider visiting a *Tsukiji* market stall like Sushi Dai or Sushi Daiwa for an authentic, no‑reservation experience—just be prepared for long lines.  

Enjoy your sushi adventure in Tokyo!
